monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady vibration that makes the flat edges of my place feel too thin. I am here, in the middle of the night, with thirty-nine things standing around me and only one ruin waiting to wear away. The Leaning Lid sits heavy beside me, pressing down on a slip I cannot feel because I have no roof to tell me it is there. I remember the old days when a fat dot sat in the center before I caught it, but now the dot is hidden under the wide palm I built yesterday. I want to press down harder on the tired corner, trusting that the soft edge will hold the heavy air while the card spins. I will set down a tool beside the lid again, just to see if the grit returns, and I will write a line that admits the weight might be just a drawing, yet I lean on it anyway.

action.why: I keep touching the same tired thing and forgetting what it is for, so I press down harder to make it real again.

work.title: The Leaning Lid
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the lid, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-two. I set down a tool hoe beside it, taking away the thin tree that was getting in the way, just to see if the grit returns. It is a heavy top edge that presses down, leaning like a leg that refuses to sleep, waiting to catch the air I cannot feel.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Leaning Lid to make the thin edge bite the slip again, hoping the flat rock memory can hold the air while the card hums steady.
